name: Lookout Mountain Lariat
_version_doc: The V3 config (2026-10-11). Nothing has been built at this version; the installed July build is 0.15.0. ui_track.json stamps '[build <version>]' so a stale install is visible at a glance.
author: k10-motorsports
_about: V3 rebuild of the Lariat (ledger 0048; tracks/lookout-lariat/V3-PLAN.md and DOSSIER.md). Kevin approved the plan's defaults on 2026-10-11 ('Those changes are good'): D1 keep the Colfax double-back; D2 (a) one slab per divided stretch, Reverse drives them against the arrows and says so; D3 (a) a race version on the real narrow road (four layouts); D4 build both edge widths for Drive 1; D5 static C-470 bridges; D6 real relief beyond ~50-100 m (the L3 amendment shared with ledger 0046) and a Denver skyline after Drive 2; D7 all five July calls reversed; A1-A13 as written. The engine drafts route-only, Claude authors in Blender, the gates judge the built file, Kevin's drive decides. P0 is done; P2 has the centreline only: data/centerline.geojson is the paint centreline (tools/paint_centreline.py, 2026-10-11; the gps stage's OSM line is kept as data/centerline.osm.geojson). No elevation, mesh, kn5 or install yet. Stations below are metres along the V3 centreline in centerline.local.json's frame from local v0 = the pylons (scripts/geometry/projection.py; on the paint centreline local index = data/centerline.geojson index + 2, because projection's own start_at pick lands two 1 m vertices before geojson v0; it was + 1 on the OSM line). Every vertex index and station here was re-derived onto the paint centreline by station matching (tools/remap_centreline_config.py; data/centerline_remap.json lists each old and new value). The paint centreline is 8.5 m longer than the OSM line, so against the dossier its stations read -1 to +14 m (most of it from C4-C6, where OSM cut the hairpins short) up to exit 259, and up to a further +20 m after it (the A1 fixes).

source._doc: The whole lap lives on the OSM road network, fetched by route.roads (named, 'ref:' and 'id:' entries) into data/osm.cache.json (query fingerprint 93e1c28d8828c2f2, fetched 2026-10-11T19:29:58Z, OSM base 2026-10-11T19:28:01Z, 197 ways). 'ref:' entries exclude motorways, so US-40 / US-6 never drag I-70 in; route.exclude_ids then drops the wrong side of two divided pieces when the payload is parsed. No KML.

centerline_frame._doc: The centreline every vertex index and station in this config refers to (its md5). tools/remap_centreline_config.py re-derives them by station matching whenever data/centerline.geojson changes, and refuses a line it cannot match to this record.

route._width_profile_doc: Rural width table in scripts/gps/widths_from_osm.py (3.0 m lanes, no urban parking/turn allowances). The real widths the dossier has are in width_overrides; the rest is measured on the aerial (dossier section 12) before the road is drawn.
route._start_at_doc: Station 0 = the two 1917 stone pylons on 19th St at the foot of the Lariat (dossier 2b). Every layout's timing line is here; each grid stands just behind it in its own direction.
route._roads_doc: Order = the ring: 19th St -> Lookout Mountain Rd (the Lariat Trail, over the top) -> Paradise Rd (Mount Vernon) -> US-40 down Mt Vernon Canyon, I-70 Business and West Colfax ('ref:US 40') -> US-6 ('ref:US 6') -> the id: entry, the US-6 off-ramp to 19th St (the lap climbs the real ramp; closing mainline-to-bridge directly made a fake 6.5 m step). A1 (Kevin, 2026-10-11): the ramp ends on its LEFT branch onto 19th St west, ways 533503210 + 1283267904 ('19th Street west;Lookout Mountain Road', turn:lanes left), not 533503214 (the right branch to 19th St east, which made a ~190 deg U-turn and ~105 m the wrong way). D1 (Kevin, default): the Colfax double-back stays, a 24.9 km lap; the in-game text says the turn is unverified.
route._exclude_ids_doc: Opt-in route key (scripts/gps/overpass.fetch_ways), applied when the payload is parsed: the query, its fingerprint and the snapshot are unchanged, and the snapshot keeps both ways for tools/route_oneway_check.py. Each id is the WRONG side of a divided piece that the stitcher keeps because it is shorter. 42005706 = exit 259's 4-lane south-west-bound side (A1: the July lap drove it 84 m against its arrows; the lap now takes the north-east-bound 119006778). 533500102 = 19th St's eastbound one-way side at the ramp terminal: with A1's ids alone the 19th St path still ran on it and the lap drove 59.6 m against its arrows (found by tools/route_oneway_check.py on 2026-10-11); dropping it puts the left turn on 1283267904 -> 1106864351 -> 533504135, the westbound side, as A1 intends. An id that is no longer in the snapshot (OSM re-split) fails the stage.
route._measured_widths_doc: P2 step 1 (scripts/gps/measured_widths.py, after scripts.gps.widths_from_osm): the aerial pass's MEASURED widths (NAIP 2019: width stations, hairpin legs, hairpin apexes) override the published width_overrides, which override the 'mountain' OSM table, per top-level width_overrides stretch; a measured width is the painted travelled way (edge-line centre to centre + one 0.10 m stripe); in a town_segments stretch with no edge lines, the curb-to-curb pavement. widths_from_osm's junction flares, hard-corner flares and 10 m fold floors are not laid (not measurements; A2 keeps hairpin widening off, P3b authors the mouths). The record is data/widths.measured.json.

hairpin_fit._doc: A2 / P2 step 2. WHERE the line runs is judged by tools/verify_centreline_paint.py against the paint traced on NAIP 2019 (data/aerial/paint_traces.json), not against OSM: the fitter's former 1.5 m-from-OSM ceiling (max_move_m) passed fits 7.3 m and 4.4 m off the paint at C4 and C10, where OSM itself cuts the hairpins, and failed C9, where OSM was right; it was removed on 2026-10-11. The Lariat's centreline is tools/paint_centreline.py's: the OSM line (data/centerline.osm.geojson) moved onto the traced paint, OSM kept where the paint is in shadow (C7's apex, C11, the upper climb), blended between, the climb resampled at 1 m as one curvature-continuous line; it is data/centerline.geojson, the file every later stage reads. tools/fit_hairpins.py stays as the clothoid-arc-clothoid library and a per-corner radius check (its step gate only). st_m = each corner's apex station on data/centerline.geojson (metres from v0, the pylons), re-found within 40 m; re-derived onto the paint centreline by station matching on 2026-10-11 (tools/remap_centreline_config.py). climb_st_m is on the OSM source line: the paint tools map it through each vertex's osm_station_m, so it is never remapped. radius_m: the aerial pass (dossier 12; NAIP 2019, data/aerial/aerial_measurements.json, reproduced by tools/aerial_measure.py) for C1-C6, C8-C10, C12 and C13; null = centreline-derived (C7: low aerial confidence; C11: not measurable on that flight); each corner's _doc says which and why. The paint centreline follows the paint, whose yellow-line circle carries each hairpin's radius; data/aerial/paint_centreline.json compares the line's tightest radius with radius_m per corner. C12 and C13 are junction nodes (one OSM node holds most of the turn); their radius_m is the aerial junction measurement, for P3b's junction mouth: an arc at that radius needs ~12.5 m tangents, but the traced arm paint (the double yellow up to the stop line) runs to within 9-15 m of the node, so the paint centreline keeps the node, on the paint-anchored arms. The ~90-111 deg bends at OSM-line st ~1,752 / 4,102 / 4,960 / 6,809 / 6,982 are not in the dossier's corner table and are not declared; the paint centreline follows their paint where it is traced (st ~6,809: OSM was 3.9 m off).

gate._doc: tools/fit_hairpins.py's step gate, on each fitted span plus join_margin untouched points either side: every heading change between consecutive points <= (spacing / R_fit) x 57.3 deg + step_slack_deg (spacing = the mean of the two segments at the point; the first term is the fitted arc's own turn per point), and adjacent heading changes differ by <= adjacent_step_deg. Both [invented] (plan P2 step 2). The same two rules, with the line's own local radius in place of R_fit, are check (b) of tools/verify_centreline_paint.py over the whole climb at 1 m. The former max_move_m (1.5 m from the OSM line) is gone: position is judged against the paint, check (a) of the same gate (0.75 m [invented]). See fleet/GATES-CHANGELOG.md, 2026-10-11 paint gate.

corners._doc: radius_m stays null: centreline-derived (18.16 m), unconfirmed. Not measurable on NAIP 2019: the apex and exit are in deep conifer shadow on a north-facing slope. Needs another image, Street View or a visit.

corners.name: Paradise Rd tee
corners._doc: kink: a junction node turns 78.5 deg, so the centreline has no radius here. radius_m: aerial, 14.9 m +-1.4 (medium): the inside kerb return is R 9.1 m (an arc tangent to both arms' inside pavement edges), and the lap arc is concentric with it at the arms' mean inside half-width (6.51 m on Lookout Mtn Rd with its wide shoulders, 5.10 m on Paradise Rd). With the 6.7 m ribbon centred on the lap, R 12.45 m would put the ribbon's inside edge on the kerb return. The dossier's 'R~13 m' depends on how far apart its three measuring points sit.

corners.name: Paradise Rd bend
corners._doc: kink: one OSM node turns 76.4 deg, so the centreline has no radius here. radius_m: aerial, 16.08 m +-1.2 (medium): the inside (SW) kerb return is R 11.4 m (tangent-constrained), plus the arms' mean inside half-width (4.38 / 4.98 m). With the 6.7 m ribbon, R 14.75 m would put its inside edge on the kerb return.

_frame_doc: The V3 loop frame used by every V3 tool: local ENU metres (x = east, y = up, z = north) about the centreline centroid, mirror_x false, true north 0 (scripts/geometry/projection.py). July built mirror_x true / true north 180; everything keyed to that frame or to July stations (AI lines, map, lights, dummies, crossfall, bridge spans) is regenerated, never reused (ledgers 0015, 0038).
_default_width_doc: The width of a vertex nothing else sets: 2 lanes averaging 3.35 m, the Lariat Trail's published average (Jeffco/FHU 2025). osm_road_widths and width_overrides set the real per-vertex widths in P2.
_osm_road_widths_doc: Per-vertex curb-to-curb widths map-matched from OSM lanes (mountain profile), overridden by width_overrides wherever the dossier has a published or measured width. The lap spans very different roads: the 6.1-6.7 m Lariat Trail, 3-lane US-40, 2-6 lane Golden streets, one 2-lane carriageway of US-6.

_width_overrides_doc: From the dossier (2a, 12): a number only where a source gives one, null + status where the aerial still has to measure it. Read in P2 by the road draft (nothing consumes this key yet). Stations are V3 local stations.

road_profile._doc: Elevation is 100 % real USGS 3DEP along the route: 1,829 m at the pylons, ~2,228 m at the Buffalo Bill lot, the lap high point 2,288 m on the back side (st ~9,150), the low point 1,783 m on US-6 (st ~23,070); 505 m of relief, ~552 m of climbing per lap (dossier 3). No authored dips or cambers.
road_profile._max_grade_doc: A7: stays at 16 %, and never binds: the steepest 20 m on the lap is -11.5 % on 1 m 3DEP (July's 'Paradise Rd -14.5 %' does not reproduce: -10.3 % over 100 m). The 6 % default 'flattened the descent and floated the road metres above the canyon floor' (July). Any change is gated on replication vs 3DEP, measured before and after.

crossfall._method_doc: scripts/elevation/crossfall.py build_footprint (P2 step 4): 3DEP pairs inside the real-width footprint only (the outermost 1.0 m inside each edge), ground beside the road used only to classify bench vs crown; the construction standard (2 % crown, or 2 % toward the cut ditch on a bench) everywhere the measurement is weaker than 2 %, over 6 %, banked into a curve, on a declared deck, or fails the roll-rate gate (tools/verify_crossfall.py: <= 4 % change per 30 m, no +3 % to -3 % swing within 30 m, both [invented]). data/crossfall.json carries status 'estimated'.
crossfall._doc: A6: the road is not tilted into the hairpins, because the real one isn't (L10; ledger 0003 stays open). July's data/crossfall.json was DEM-estimated, not measured (~10 % of stations sat at its 6 % cap, 19 % on US-40; 9 swings of >= 3 % each way within 30 m), and is not reused. P2 re-measures inside the real-width footprint with a roll-rate gate; until a 3DEP source-lidar sample agrees it is 'estimated', and failing stretches take the construction standard: 2 % crown, or 2 % toward the cut ditch on bench sections.

road_profile._verge_doc: D4 (Kevin 2026-10-11: build both, pick by driving). The strip beside the pavement: A = 0.4 m (real width, then the real edge: rock cut, ditch or drop; 0.3-0.5 m gravel); B = 1.25 m (a 1-1.5 m firm gravel strip you can put a wheel on). Both builds are in drive1_variants. Replaces July's 6.4 m drivable 'shoulder' per side (22.6 m drivable in all, against the real 6.1-6.7 m). No rumble lips in either.

gates._doc: Per-track gate values for the Lariat's Drive-1 set (V3-PLAN P5, ledger 0048). Read by the gates themselves; every other track has no such block, so its gates run exactly as before. Each value carries its tag; fleet/GATES-CHANGELOG.md has the entry.

drive_test._kinks_doc: [std: measured on reference mountain roads] (fleet/reference/MEASURED.md section 8, 2026-10-12): drive_test's own kink metric (slope change > 3 %-points between consecutive 1 m steps, six interior wheel paths) run by tools/calibrate_kinks.py on four reference mountain roads on this machine: simtraxx Pikes Peak pp100ahc 19.49/km (20.0 km), la_canyons mt_wilson_hillclimb 0.73/km (6.8 km), simtraxx Targa Florio stage 1 0.49/km (14.2 km), la_canyons angeles_crest_east 0.00/km (40.9 km). The ceiling is the kinkiest of them: a Lariat that reads more is kinkier than every reference mountain road. It replaces the plan's 5/km [invented: Lake Murray V3's own 4.97/km]. Kinks gate nowhere else (scripts/geometry/drive_test.py reads this key only when a track declares it).

stacked_legs._doc: tools/verify_stacked_legs.py's thresholds are module constants (pairs < 40 m in plan and > 150 m along the lap, 0 failures, all [invented]); a 'classes' map here would override which built groups count as ground / edge / sign / closure (none set: the tool's defaults). Measured on the paint centreline with July's 3DEP corridor samples (2026-10-12): 10,659 pairs at 1 m on 680 lap points in 12 stacked runs (st 2,493-3,152 Tiers of Zion, 5,305-5,996 the upper hairpins), nearest 21.3 m in plan, vertical gap 6.49-14.90 m (median 9.98 m); no crossing.

drive1._doc: tools/drive1_gates.py: V3-PLAN P5's Drive-1 gate set, judged on the gate reports of one build (data/drive1_gates.json; gating vs recorded rows). Every value is P5's, tagged as P5 tags it; fleet/GATES-CHANGELOG.md 2026-10-12 'Drive-1 verdict'. The kink ceiling is gates.drive_test.kinks_per_km_max.

drive_test._severe_doc: [invented] P5: severe steps (>= 6 cm, drive_test's own STEP_SEVERE_M, itself a flagged value) 0 per street layout; drive_test's own line is > 12/km.
drive_test._replication_doc: [invented in 0048] P5: the built road against the raw 3DEP profile, p95 <= 0.5 m.
drive_test._zero_doc: soft-top in lane, obstruction, floating furniture, undrivable corners, daylight gaps: 0 each [std: drive_test's existing count gates] (constants in the tool, not values here).

audit._doc: P5: hard classes A B D E G H I = 0 [std: audit_mesh's existing hard total]; F (curb not flush) <= 15 [invented: Lake Murray V3's own count]. J / K at the race-turn mouths are Drive 3. The street audit's own exit (hard total, F at 0) also gates in tools/ship_track.sh.

kn5_ground_check._doc: P5: road over ground p95 <= 0.10 m [std: the existing gate] (kn5_ground_check's own verdict); the lid: no step > 0.10 m at either end [invented in 0048], read from drive_test's severe-step list within 5 m of each end of capture.bridges.

july_reference._doc: [measured on the installed July v0.46.0 build] (V3-PLAN P5 '--force-install rule', 0047): a red street run may still install with --force-install only if no worse than these on every key; obstruction, floating furniture and soft-top are always 0. tools/ship_track.sh refuses a forced install when data/drive1_gates.json force_install_ok is false.

drive1_variants._doc: D4: two Drive-1 installs, identical apart from road_profile.verge_m. tools/ship_track.sh builds one per run: SHIP_VARIANT=<id> (unset = this config as written, i.e. a_real_edge) passes --variant to scripts/blender/underlay.py (the edge strip, in memory: the config file is never rewritten), installs into the variant's install_folder under its ui_name_prefix, refuses to prep a loop.blend whose GEN_verge (data/underlay.json) is the other variant's, and never syncs a variant run's outputs back into airoso.

road_text._doc: No painted street-name decals — they land in the wrong places on this rural loop (Kevin), and mountain roads don't have them anyway.

road_markings._doc: Double yellow the whole way up the Lariat (20 mph, dossier 2a) plus white edge lines; Golden's own markings (19th St bike lanes and flex posts, crosswalks) are authored in P3i.

kerb._doc: No racing kerbs anywhere. July's curvature test lined 25 km of a 6.5 m lane with 5 cm vertical-lip rumble strips, Kevin's 'undriveable slop'. Real curbs and sidewalks in Golden are authored where they are real (A9, P3i), not drawn by this engine switch.

runoff._doc: No tarmac run-off on a pitched mountainside: the edge is rock cut, fill, stone, W-beam or open ground (scenery.edges).

divided._doc: D2 (a), Kevin 2026-10-11: each divided stretch is ONE slab carrying both sides and the real median (ledger 0037's pattern), never a second ribbon. Every layout drives the lap's side, the Full direction's, with the arrows; Street Reverse drives all four against the arrows and its ui text says so. 'ways' = the lap's side, which route_oneway_check reads as Reverse's declared exceptions; 'other_side_ways' = the opposite one-way carriageway beside it, for the slab (P3e) and the race closures (P3j). Derived 2026-10-11 by tools/route_oneway_check.py on the V3 centreline + data/osm.cache.json. 19th St is 54 m on its westbound side (the dossier's 105 m was the eastbound side the July line drove); the left-turn branch 1283267904 (6 m) is counted with the ramp.

stretches.name: I-70 Business at exit 259: the 2-lane north-east-bound side (A1)
West Colfax Ave: its one-way piece before the US-6 signal
US-6, the Golden-bound carriageway, plus its off-ramp and the left-turn branch onto 19th St
19th St at the ramp terminal: the westbound side

bridges._doc: P2 step 5 (V3-PLAN; ledger 0048). Decks on the lap are DECLARED from evidence, never left to a detector. scripts/elevation/road_profile.py finds each declared deck's stretch of the lap over its footprint ways (each OSM way's centreline buffered by half its pavement width, route.width_profile), adds abutment_m each side, holds the road straight across it in the raw 3DEP profile before smoothing, writes data/bridge.spans.json, and with --write records it as capture.bridges (local stations), the engine's declared-span key.
bridges._l13_seam_rule_doc: Opt-in for scripts/geometry/build_mesh.py's height detector (_bridge_detector, the one that minted July's [24,278-24,803]): on a closed lap a run that reaches the closing vertex while vertex 0 is not on a span is a wrap artefact (L13) and is dropped. Other tracks keep the detector as it was. The V3 Lariat does not run build_mesh; the prep's OSM-way detector (scripts/ac/build_kn5_loop.py detect_bridge_spans) gets the same rule unconditionally.

declared._doc: The 19th St lid over the US-6 tunnel (OSM ways 533503591 + 533679737, tunnel=yes, layer -1, 2 lanes each): the lap's stretch over the two tunnel footprints plus 8 m of abutment each side [invented: the prep's BRIDGE_PAD_M], held straight. ~550 m before the pylons, clear of the seam (L13).

dropped.why: July auto span (engine v0.46.0 build_mesh height detector, 24,802.6 m built frame): 525 m ending on the lap's last vertex without continuing from vertex 0, a wrap artefact (L13); holding it level would erase 19th St's real +5.7 % climb. The only structure in that stretch is the lid, declared above from its footprint. No V3 lap way there carries bridge=yes (data/bridge.spans.json lap_osm_bridge_ways).

July auto span containing the C-470 crossing on US-6 (aerial: C-470 way 84720905 crosses OVER the lap at OSM-line st 21,137.6, its deck measured across the lap in data/aerial/aerial_measurements.json c470): the lap passes UNDER a bridge there, not over one. No V3 lap way there carries bridge=yes.

layouts.name: Street — Full
layouts._start_doc: Ledger 0047's declared start, as vertices into data/centerline.local.json (its own index space: local v0 = the pylons). line_vertex 0 = AC_TIME_0 at the pylons. Forward grid v14417 = 27.0 m behind the line on 19th St; reverse grid v26 = 26.0 m behind it on Lookout Mountain Rd (layout_dummies: 0 < d <= 35 m). Sectors on straight vertices (kink < 1 deg over +/-6 vertices): v7185 near the summit (st 7187.3) and v11623 on US-40 just before exit 259 (st 16564.0), so the three sectors are the climb, the top + canyon, and Golden. Validated 2026-10-11 by tools/layout_dummies.py on a plan-only projection of this centreline; re-run on the real centerline.local.json in P4. offset_right_m 1.6 = the right-hand lane's centre on a ~6.5 m two-lane road, PROVISIONAL: the width at the pylons is not measured (dossier 12). With layout_dummies' +/-1.0 m grid stagger the outer column's car edge sits 3.55 m right of centre, past the edge of a 6.5 m road; re-set it from the aerial width (or single-file the grid) in P4.
layouts.run: anticlockwise: from the pylons up the Lariat Trail, over the top past Buffalo Bill, Paradise Rd, down Mt Vernon Canyon on US-40, home through Golden on I-70 Business, Colfax, US-6 and 19th St
layouts.ui_description: Street — Full: 24.9 km of open two-way roads, anticlockwise seen from above. From the 1917 stone pylons on 19th St up the 1913 Lariat Trail's stacked hairpins (20 mph, double yellow, about 6.5 m wide), over Lookout Mountain past Buffalo Bill's grave, down Paradise Rd and Mt Vernon Canyon on US-40, and home through Golden on I-70 Business, Colfax, US-6 and its 19th St ramp, every one-way with its arrows. At the US-6/Colfax signal the lap turns back on itself (152 deg); whether that turn is legal there is unverified. Real roads from OpenStreetMap at real USGS 3DEP elevation; nothing closed. The AI line is a generated draft, not an in-game recording.
layouts._doc: Kevin's 'Full' (D3 a): the July layout id 'full' is renamed because tools/layout_dummies.validate_layouts refuses 'full' and 'freeroam' (track_folder drops the Content Manager name suffix for them). direction is the flag every tool keys on, never the id.

layouts.name: Street — Reverse

layouts.ui_description: Street — Reverse: the same 24.9 km driven the other way, clockwise seen from above: 19th St, the US-6 off-ramp and US-6, Colfax, I-70 Business, up Mt Vernon Canyon on US-40, Paradise Rd, over the top and down the Lariat Trail's hairpins to the pylons. It drives four one-way pieces of divided road against their arrows, about 4.5 km in all: the US-6 carriageway with its off-ramp (4.0 km), 312 m of West Colfax, 54 m of 19th St at the ramp and 86 m at I-70 exit 259; the other side of each is beside you, not driven. At the US-6/Colfax signal the lap turns back on itself (152 deg); whether that turn is legal there is unverified. Real roads from OpenStreetMap at real USGS 3DEP elevation. The AI line is a generated draft, not an in-game recording.

layouts_parked.name: Race — Anticlockwise
layouts_parked._start_doc: As street_full's _start_doc. offset_right_m 0.0: a one-way race uses the whole road, so the grid is centred (columns at +/-1.0 m, car edges 1.95 m from centre, inside a 6.1 m road).
layouts_parked.run: anticlockwise, one-way: up the Lariat Trail, over the top, Paradise Rd, down Mt Vernon Canyon, home through Golden; the whole mountain road edge to edge
layouts_parked.ui_description: Race — Anticlockwise: the Full direction as a closed one-way race on the real roads. The whole mountain road is yours edge to edge (about half Alvarado's width on the climb), with its real stone, steel and open edges and nothing added in it or along it. Every side road is barriered at its edge; the full intersection is open at the five corners where the race turns (the Paradise Rd tee, Paradise Rd onto US-40, exit 259, Colfax onto US-6, the ramp onto 19th St); Golden's multi-lane streets are narrowed to about Alvarado's width; on each divided road you race one side and the other is closed off. The AI line is a generated draft, not an in-game recording.

layouts_parked._start_doc: As street_reverse's (grid v26, sectors reversed); offset_right_m 0.0: centred grid on the whole one-way road.
layouts_parked.run: clockwise, one-way: 19th St, US-6, Colfax, up Mt Vernon Canyon, Paradise Rd, over the top and down the Lariat Trail; the whole mountain road edge to edge

race._doc: D3 (a), Kevin 2026-10-11: a race version on the real narrow road (dossier 4c), on the corridor rules of ledgers 0047 / 0049 (Lake Murray) adapted to this road: Kevin's brief asks for 'more or less an Alvarado's width for the entire track with deviances in various areas'; on the Lariat the deviation is most of the lap, because every layout drives the same road surface (L8) and the mountain road is 6.1-6.7 m. Read by the race tools AFTER P1 adapts them (SD's hard-coded STREETS become this block, SD byte-identical). Today's tools/barrier_bands.py is Lake Murray's and refuses this block loudly (no single 'whole' interval, no pinned closure_runs, clear_width_source is not a street in route.roads).
rules: 1. The 6-7 m two-lane mountain road is used whole, one-way: closing 'the other lane' would leave a 3 m strip.

2. No K-rail down the historic road and no barrier added along its edges: the real edges (1913 stone, W-beam, open) are the race edges. No race kerbs on the mountain (Kevin's July 'undriveable slop').
3. Closures go at junction edges; curb-line barriers only where a real curb line exists, on Golden's streets.

race._edge_mode_doc: Not Lake Murray's 'road' mode (strips along both curbs of every street): on this road the real edges are the race edges (rule 2); curb-line barriers only on Golden's streets where the survey shows a real curb line.
race._barrier_doc: Kevin's 4 m K-rail silhouette, swept as strips (Lake Murray's race pattern). Its licence is UNRECORDED, so the race kn5s stay in the Full package, as on Lake Murray (A12).

kerbs._doc: No race kerbs on the mountain (rule 2); none in town until Kevin asks.

lighting._presets_doc: The climb faces east / north-east, so mornings light the switchbacks with the plains in haze below (the money shot); by late afternoon the east face goes into shadow first (dossier 7).

streetlight._doc: D7 item 1 reversed (Kevin 2026-10-11): lamps only where they really stand (scenery.lamps); the mountain and the canyon are dark. His July pool SHAPE stays ('~3x spread, no ground saturation': range 60, spot 155, sharpness 0.1, gradient offset 0.55, specular 0.12). Colour: high-pressure sodium, the type OSM tags on 24 of the 25 typed lamps (ledger 0043's HPS line 255,183,76 with single_frequency 0.7; San Diego's low-pressure finding does not transfer). Intensity in the 255-scale decade (ledger 0043: CSP multiplies the 0-255 colour by intensity with no /255; July's 0.35 was an effective 89). 0.010 is 0043's soft-sodium start; ladder if too dark 0.015 -> 0.020, ceiling 0.03; if the 60 m pools read hot, step down toward 0.006. The 0043 soft keys (diffuse concentration, half-res blurred shadows, no volumetric, no long specular, fade 800/200) are copied. emissive 0.5 = the low end of 0043's band for an authored lamp head (Kevin's lamp_lens.obj is a visible head).

light_pollution._doc: The night glow is Denver's, on the eastern horizon, and matches the HPS lamps (la_canyons ships 255,183,76). relative_position biases it east: in the kn5 frame with mirror_x false, +x is east; the magnitude copies the writer default's (~2) and CSP's units are unverified, so VERIFY at the Drive 2 night row. density / radius_km stay at the writer defaults.

grassfx._doc: Ledger 0045's grammar (scripts/environment/treefx.grassfx_block). D7 item 3: tawny late-summer foothill grass, unmown, from 0045's deferred straw-slope settings (SHAPE_SIZE 0.7-1.2, SHAPE_WIDTH 0.5, TRIM_PERIOD 365). mask 'open' so blades certainly appear on first load. Blades take the ground texel's colour, so the tawny look rides on the ground texture (texture_overrides). The writer binds only 1GRASS* meshes: the corridor and medium terrain tiers. The view / far / plains tiers carry no digit prefix and rock cuts and wall faces are their own meshes, so no grass grows there. LADDERS (config only): patchier -> mask 'default' + mask_blur 1; too tall -> shape_size [0.6, 1.0]; neon under the lamps at night -> texture_brightness 0.8; off without losing the tuning -> enabled false.

terrain._doc: P3a terrain tiers (dossier 6d, V3-PLAN P3a). D6 (i), Kevin 2026-10-11: real relief beyond the road. Near the road (out to ~60-100 m) the ground stays shaped to the road; beyond that it blends back to its real surveyed 3DEP height within a few hundred metres, so Clear Creek Canyon below Wildcat Point and Golden below Windy Saddle exist. This needs the one-line amendment to rule L3 (today: all ground within 22 m of the nearest road's height), shared with ledger 0046 (Lake Murray's Cowles Mountain). The amendment is NOT yet written into fleet/LAWS.md: config and plan only now, no geometry.

l3_amendment.status: approved by Kevin 2026-10-11 (D6 i); not yet in fleet/LAWS.md

cross_section._doc: docs/ROAD-CONSTRUCTION.md's Lariat section, uphill to downhill. Between stacked hairpin legs the default is cut + fill, not walls (A3): the legs sit >= 13.8 m apart edge to edge at real width with 6.5-14.7 m between them vertically, and the section closes 13 m of height in 11 m. A wall only where the survey shows one (Wildcat Point's two battered walls, the Windy Saddle walls, the stone guardrails' footings) or where the section cannot close; those are AUTH_wall_authored_* and listed for Kevin.

stacked_legs._doc: On the July line: 1,188 pairs at st ~2,500-2,950 and ~5,300-5,850, vertical gap 6.5-14.7 m, nearest 20.5 m on the map; re-measured on the V3 line in P2. [invented] thresholds, V3-PLAN P5.

skyline._doc: a low-poly Denver skyline extruded from OSM building heights at its real bearing, 19.6-23.2 km east, one visual-only mesh in the backdrop kn5 (sourced, so L1 allows it); visible from the lower hairpins up, blocked from the pylons by South Table Mountain's shoulder

scenery._doc: V3 never runs the engine's environment stage (scripts/environment/build_env.py): no I-70 / C-470 decks (the 'wavy ribbons', ~40 km of 22 m deck, ledger 0048), no sine-wave MOUNTAINS, no creek ribbons, no unverified power-line run, no baked forest. Each block below is read by a V3 authoring tool (V3-PLAN P1-P3).

treefx._doc: A8 + D7 item 5 reversed (Kevin 2026-10-11): trees where the real forest is, zoned by which way the slope faces and by band (dossier 6a), densest on the north-facing upper hairpins and opening into ponderosa woodland over the top; NOT July's 'more trees the higher up' (sparse at the base, densest at the summit). North- and east-facing slopes carry conifers; south- and west-facing are open grass and shrub. Read by tools/make_treefx.py once P1 adapts it to take zones, species and ground tiles from config. Every model is third-party mod content (personal use): it rides in the Full package only; the public zip ships no vegetation (A12). Corridor guard: no tree within half-width + 1 m of any centreline (ledger 0040).
treefx._density_doc: Trees per 10 m ground cell (make_treefx's fill grammar), on conifer-aspect cells; open-aspect cells take conifers at open_conifer_factor and shrubs instead. [authored] starting points: the dossier gives the classes, not numbers; tuned in Drive 2.

Never: Gambel oak, pinyon, anything urban on the mountain.

The Lariat (st 1,073-7,102), the back side, Paradise Rd and the US-40 canyon have none: the mountain and the canyon are dark. Night stays available. tools/lamp_inventory.py (new, P3h) turns the surveyed list into data/lights.local.json; tools/author_lamps_blend.py (adapted) takes those positions with a height per lamp. A Street View pass decides which edge is which, run by run (dossier 12); where the survey is silent a drop-height rule decides and the run is labelled authored. ui_description: A 24.9 km lap built on the Lariat Trail, Golden, Colorado: up the 1913 Lariat Trail's stacked hairpins from the 1917 stone pylons, over Lookout Mountain past Buffalo Bill's grave, down Mt Vernon Canyon and home through Golden. Real roads from OpenStreetMap at real USGS 3DEP elevation.
_ui_description_doc: Track-level fallback; each layout carries its own. Not 'the Lariat Loop' (the ~40 mile byway leaves the mountain westward); no Nordschleife comparison, no 'most photographed corners' (dossier 1).
readme_about: Real roads from OpenStreetMap at real USGS 3DEP elevation, 24.9 km a lap: the 1913 Lariat Trail up Lookout Mountain from Golden's 1917 stone pylons, the summit, Paradise Rd, US-40 down Mt Vernon Canyon, and Golden's I-70 Business, Colfax, US-6 and 19th St.
_ui_tags_doc: The installed July ui carried 'fictional' (an old engine default); this is a real road. track_folder adds 'circuit' on a loop so Content Manager allows Race / Track Day sessions.
_install_folder_doc: A11: every file inside is lookout_lariat; the folder on this machine is lookout_lariat_v3 while the July build stays installed (July is parked only after V3 reaches T3, three clean laps each way); the release zip's folder is lookout_lariat, so it replaces the old public copy. Drive 1's verge variant installs as lookout_lariat_v3_verge (drive1_variants).
